included.name: Interpreted Execution
included.description: Python code is executed by an interpreter, supporting scripting and rapid prototyping.

included.name: Portability and Readability
included.description: Python runs on multiple platforms and uses syntax designed to be relatively readable and concise.

included.name: Command Syntax
included.description: Python uses new lines to end commands rather than requiring statement-ending semicolons.

included.name: Indentation and Scope
included.description: Python uses indentation to mark the scope of constructs such as loops, functions, and classes.

included.name: Comments
included.description: Comments are notes in source code that the interpreter does not execute.

included.name: Indentation and Comments
included.description: Python uses indentation to define code blocks, and `#` begins a comment that is not executed.

included.name: Variables
included.description: Variables are names used to refer to values in a program.

included.name: Data Types
included.description: Data types identify kinds of values and affect which operations can be performed on them.

included.name: Dynamic Typing
included.description: Python determines types at runtime rather than requiring variables to have declared types.

included.name: Print Function
included.description: Python’s built-in `print()` function displays values or messages on the screen or in the console.

included.name: User Input
included.description: The `input()` function reads text entered by a user.

included.name: Type Conversion
included.description: Built-in functions can convert values from one data type to another.

included.name: Arithmetic Operators
included.description: Arithmetic operators perform calculations such as addition, division, and exponentiation.

included.name: Assignment Operators
included.description: Assignment operators set or update the value associated with a variable.

included.name: Augmented Assignment
included.description: Augmented assignment operators such as `+=` update a variable using a compact assignment expression.

included.name: Operator Precedence
included.description: Operator precedence determines the order in which parts of an expression are evaluated.

included.name: Comparison Operators
included.description: Comparison operators compare values and produce boolean results.

included.name: Logical Operators
included.description: The `and`, `or`, and `not` operators combine or invert logical conditions.

included.name: Bitwise Operators
included.description: Bitwise operators perform operations on the binary representations of values.

included.name: High-Level Data Structures
included.description: Python provides efficient, high-level structures for organizing and working with data.

included.name: Strings
included.description: Strings represent textual data and are written inside quotes.

included.name: String Concatenation
included.description: String concatenation combines strings into a single string, commonly using the `+` operator.

included.name: String Methods
included.description: String methods perform operations such as changing case, finding text, or replacing text.

included.name: String Immutability
included.description: Strings cannot be changed in place, so operations that appear to modify them return new strings.

included.name: Membership Operator
included.description: The `in` operator checks whether an item or sequence occurs within a string.

included.name: Lists
included.description: Lists store multiple items in an ordered sequence using square brackets.

included.name: Conditional Statements
included.description: `if`, `elif`, and `else` branches select which code block runs based on conditions.

included.name: For Loops
included.description: A `for` loop runs a block once for each item in a sequence or range.

included.name: While Loops
included.description: A `while` loop repeats a block as long as its condition remains true.
